purpose: Equipment-class domain knowledge for LLM-based OEE Loss Analysis. Provides mechanical/process context so the agent can reason about failure modes, bottlenecks, and degradation signatures specific to each machine class rather than generically.

machine_profiles.machine_purpose: Forms, blanks, or draws sheet metal (or performs progressive-die stamping) into net-shape or near-net-shape components using mechanical or hydraulic force, typically integrated with a coil feed/straightener system for continuous strip processing.
critical_components: Mechanical or hydraulic drive system (flywheel, clutch-brake or hydraulic power unit)
Die set (upper/lower tooling, punches, blanks, cams)
Coil feed system (uncoiler, straightener, servo feed rolls)
Safety systems (light curtains, two-hand controls, interlocked guarding)
common_failure_modes: Clutch-brake wear leading to inconsistent stop position or slippage
Die/tooling wear, chipping, or breakage (punches, cutting edges)
Feed roll slippage or coil misalignment causing part mislocation
Hydraulic seal leaks causing pressure loss and ram drift
Ram/guide bearing wear causing increased clearance and part variation
Light curtain or safety interlock misalignment causing nuisance stops
Tonnage monitor false trips from miscalibration
typical_error_codes: DT-05 (SPM reduction from die wear/feed hesitation)
DT-06 (startup scrap during die thermal stabilization)
machine_profiles.expected_operating_behaviour: Consistent strokes-per-minute (SPM) matching the rated press speed for the die set in use; a repeatable tonnage curve shape stroke-to-stroke; consistent, uninterrupted part ejection and coil feed advance; stable pilot/sensor signals confirming correct strip position each cycle.
common_production_bottlenecks: Die changeover time, especially on multi-model lines without quick-die-change (QDC) systems
Coil feed interruptions from splice welds or coil-end transitions
Tonnage monitor trips requiring manual reset and root-cause check before resuming
Scrap/slug buildup in the die requiring line stop for manual clearing
Progressive die station imbalance causing localized wear-driven stoppages
maintenance_checklist: Inspect die cutting edges and forming surfaces for wear/sharpness
Lubricate ram guides and gibs per schedule
Check hydraulic fluid level, condition, and filter status
Inspect clutch-brake wear indicators and air pressure (mechanical press)
Function-test light curtains and safety interlocks
Calibrate tonnage monitoring system against known reference load
Inspect feed roll condition and pinch-roll pressure
Check coil straightener roll alignment
performance_degradation_indicators: Declining strokes-per-minute (SPM) trend vs. rated speed for the die
Rising frequency of feed hesitation or feed-fault events
Increasing time between coil splices or feed re-registration events
quality_degradation_indicators: Increasing burr height on blanked/pierced edges
Dimensional drift on formed features (radius, depth, flatness)
Increased incomplete forms or flash on drawn/formed parts
Growing part-to-part thickness or dimensional variability within a coil run
Upward trend in scrap rate correlated with die stroke count since last sharpening

machine_profiles.machine_purpose: Performs subtractive machining of precision metal or plastic components via multi-axis (typically 3- to 5-axis) rotating cutting tools, executing programmed toolpaths (G-code) to achieve dimensional tolerances and surface finish requirements not achievable via forming processes.
critical_components: Ball screws and linear guideways (X/Y/Z and rotary axes)
Automatic tool changer (ATC) and tool magazine
common_failure_modes: Spindle bearing wear or failure (heat, vibration, reduced accuracy)
Tool breakage mid-cut (chip load exceedance, tool wear beyond limit)
Ball screw backlash increasing due to wear, degrading positional accuracy
ATC misindex or tool-change failure (gripper wear, pot misalignment)
Coolant pump failure or coolant concentration drift affecting tool life
Encoder/feedback fault causing following error or axis fault
Progressive tool wear degrading surface finish before scheduled replacement
typical_error_codes: DT-03 (tool and fixture changeover, program load)
DT-05 (feed override reduction from tool wear or thermal compensation)
DT-06 (first-part thermal growth error after cold start)
DT-07 (in-process dimensional drift from progressive tool wear)
machine_profiles.expected_operating_behaviour: Programmed feed rate override held at or near 100%; stable spindle load current at a given commanded feed and depth of cut; cycle time tracking within a tight tolerance band of the NC program's estimated cycle time; consistent tool-change duration per changeover event.
common_production_bottlenecks: Tool changeover frequency, particularly for parts requiring many distinct tools
Program inefficiency — excessive air-cutting/rapid traverse time not optimized out of the toolpath
Fixture load/unload (part handling) time relative to machining time
In-process/post-process inspection dwell time (probing cycles, CMM queue)
Tool life management — reactive replacement causing unplanned mid-run stops
maintenance_checklist: Monitor spindle vibration and bearing temperature trend
Check way lubrication (oil) system function and reservoir level
Verify coolant concentration (refractometer) and fluid level/cleanliness
Inspect tool holder tapers and pull studs for cleanliness/damage
Measure axis backlash and compare to specification
Function-test ATC tool-change cycle (grip, index, exchange)
Review encoder/feedback diagnostics for following-error trends
Inspect and clean way covers and telescopic covers for chip ingress
performance_degradation_indicators: Feed override consistently trimmed below 100% by the operator to protect tool/finish
Actual cycle time creeping above the NC program's estimated cycle time
Spindle load trending upward over time at a constant commanded feed and depth of cut
Increasing frequency of tool-wear compensation offset adjustments
quality_degradation_indicators: Surface finish (Ra) degrading progressively within a tool's life
Dimensional drift within a single tool's production window (before scheduled change)
Increasing frequency of tool-wear compensation triggers on in-process probing
Scrap/rework concentration correlated with specific tool numbers or spindle hours
Rising chatter/vibration marks on machined surfaces

machine_profiles.machine_purpose: Performs sequential joining, fastening, and verification of components into sub-assemblies or finished products across multiple linked workstations, combining manual labor, semi-automated tooling (torque guns, robots/cobots), and in-line quality verification (vision, force/torque monitoring).
critical_components: Torque tools and torque control system
Vision inspection systems (presence/absence, alignment, barcode/DMC verification)
PLC line controller and station-level I/O
Component feeders (vibratory bowl, kitted parts presentation)
common_failure_modes: Conveyor jam or pallet/belt misalignment
Feeder starvation from upstream supply interruption or jam in the feed track
Torque tool calibration drift causing false pass/fail results
Vision system false reject or false accept from lighting drift or lens contamination
Sensor misalignment causing part-presence detection errors
Fixture/tooling wear causing misassembly or increased force required to mate parts
typical_error_codes: DT-04 (small stops/jams — the dominant loss category on assembly lines)
DT-05 (line speed derate to protect quality or manage a chronic station issue)
DT-07 (in-process defects — failed torque checks, vision rejects, missing components)
machine_profiles.expected_operating_behaviour: Consistent takt time achieved across all stations with the line balanced so no single station is a chronic bottleneck; low and stable WIP buffer levels between stations; torque and vision verification pass rates near 100% with minimal repeat-check events.
common_production_bottlenecks: Station with the longest cycle time relative to line takt (the line-balance constraint/bottleneck station)
Component starvation at feeders due to upstream kitting or supply chain variability
Rework loop congestion when failed-check units queue faster than they can be reworked
Model/variant changeover time on mixed-model lines
Operator-paced manual stations subject to fatigue-driven cycle time variability
maintenance_checklist: Check conveyor belt tension, tracking, and alignment
Clean and verify alignment of photo-eyes/proximity sensors at each station
Verify torque tool calibration against a certified reference (torque audit)
Clean vision system lenses and re-verify lighting/calibration settings
Inspect feeder tracks and bowl feeders for wear or blockage points
Function-test poka-yoke devices to confirm they still prevent the intended error condition
Inspect pallet/fixture locating pins and clamps for wear
performance_degradation_indicators: Increasing micro-stop frequency concentrated at one or more specific stations
Takt time creep across the line without a corresponding hard-stop event
Growing WIP buffer accumulating immediately before the constraint/bottleneck station
Rising number of manual interventions per shift at a given station
quality_degradation_indicators: Declining First Pass Yield (FPY) at final test or in-line verification stations
Increasing torque check failure rate (over-torque, under-torque, cross-thread)
Rising vision-system reject rate not attributable to lighting/calibration drift
Increasing field or warranty claims traceable to a specific assembly station or shift
Growth in the rework/repair loop queue length
